questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old female presents to the OPD with fever, lower abdominal pain and purulent vaginal discharge. On examination, her vitals are stable and per vaginal examination reveals lower abdominal and cervical motion tenderness. What is the best treatment option for her?
options: Oral doxycycline 100 mg BD with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
Oral ofloxacin 200 mg BD with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days
Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral metronidazole 400 mg for 7 days
Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Single IM injection of ceftriaxone 250 mg with oral doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days

The given clinical scenario of fever and lower abdominal pain associated with lower abdominal and cervical motion tenderness is suggestive of PID (Pelvic inflammatory disease). The best treatment option for this patient is outpatient treatment with a single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg + oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days.

Outpatient treatment of PID (according to the current RCOG guidelines):

• A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg + oral doxycycline 100 mg BD +/- metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days
• A single dose of IM ceftriaxone 250 mg followed by azithromycin 1 gm per week x 2 weeks.

Treatment of PID in hospitalized patients:

• Cefotetan 2 g IV 12hourly + doxycycline 100 mg BD orally/ IV  for 48 hours is given followed by oral doxycycline 100 mg +/- metronidazole 400 mg for 14 days
• Cefoxitin 2 g IV 6hourly + doxycycline 100 mg IV followed by oral route.
• Azithromycin 500 mg IV 6 hourly for 2 days, then orally for Chlamydia.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman with a history of how many births are referred to as a grand multipara?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. > 4

A pregnant woman with a history of >4 births is referred to as a grand multipara.

Terminologies used in pregnancy:

Gravida indicates the number of times a female has been pregnant. It includes present as well as past pregnancy, irrespective of the period of gestation.

Para indicates the number of previous pregnancies that had progressed beyond the period of viability (28 weeks of gestation or more).

1. A nullipara is one who has never completed a pregnancy to the stage of viability. She may or may not have aborted previously.
2. A nulligravida is one who is not now and never has been pregnant.
3. A primipara is one who has delivered one viable child. Parity is not increased even if the fetuses are many (twins, triplets).
4. A primigravida is one who is pregnant for the first time.
5. A multigravida is one who has previously been pregnant. She may have aborted or have delivered a viable baby.
6. A multipara is one who has completed two or more pregnancies to the stage of viability or more. A pregnant woman with a previous history of more than four births is called a grand multipara.

questions.text: At what point do you begin plotting on a partogram when the first contractions occur?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Before the alert line

In a partograph, labor is graphed and analysis includes use of action lines and alert lines.

A partograph was designed by WHO for use in developing countries. Partograph is similar for nulliparas and multiparas.

Active phase starts at 3cm cervical dilatation and progress should be no slower than 1cm/hour.

A 4 hour wait is recommended before intervention when the active phase is slow.

In the modified partograph, there is no plotting of the latent phase. The partograph is plotted once active labor begins.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Serum beta hCG testing is required to diagnose which of the following conditions?
options: Pregnancy associated with Neural tube defects
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Molar Pregnancy

Repeated serum beta hCG testing is done for a molar pregnancy.

Follow-up after the termination of molar pregnancy is done with serum β hCG levels. During the follow-up period, pregnancy must be avoided as it might interfere with the β hCG levels.

The initial β-hCG level is obtained 48 hours after evacuation and used as a baseline.

It is measured weekly till it becomes negative, and three consecutive normal values are obtained. This normally happens in 4-8 weeks.

After this, β hCG levels are measured monthly for 6 months. Women who undergo chemotherapy must be followed up for 1 year.

Other options:

Options A and B: Downs syndrome and Pregnancy associated with Neural tube defects require Maternal serum AFP testing but not serum Beta hCG testing.

Option D: Rh-negative pregnancy requires Coombs antibody testing.

questions.text: A 25-year-old primigravida presented at term with a USG report suggesting fetus in breech position and on per vaginal examination, toes of the foot can be felt. What is the next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Terminate by cesarean section

The given clinical vignette suggests that the fetus is in a footling breech position, which is an indication for a cesarean section.

In footling breech, one or both legs are extended at the hip, so that the foot is the presenting part.

A major complication of breech presentation is cord prolapse. In the cord prolapse, the umbilical cord drops down below the presenting part of the baby and becomes compressed.

Factors favoring cesarean delivery of the breech fetus:

• Large fetus: > 3800 to 4000 g
• Apparently healthy and viable preterm fetus either with active labor or with indicated delivery
• Severe IUGR
• Footling presentation (due to risk of cord prolapse)
• Hyperextended head
• Contracted pelvis
• Prior cesarean delivery
• Preterm breech
• Primi with breech
• Twins, with the first baby in the breech

Other options:

Option A: Intrernal podalic version is a maneuver used only in the delivery of a second twin. (Option A)

Option C: External cephalic version is a maneuver used before labor in a woman who has reached 36 weeks’ gestation with a breech fetus. (Option C)

Option D: Assisted breech delivery is performed when there are no factors favoring cesarean delivery of the breech fetus. (Option D)

• Complete: Breech with flexed legs

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year-old woman with a twin pregnancy at 24 weeks of gestation came for a regular antenatal check-up. She has had an abortion at 12 weeks of gestation five years back and healthy twins were delivered at term three years ago. Which of the following is the correct representation of her obstetric score?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. G3P1A1L2

This woman has had three pregnancies in total (previous abortion, previous twin pregnancy, and current twin pregnancy) with the first pregnancy aborted in the first trimester (12 weeks) and the second pregnancy resulting in the delivery of twins at term. Therefore, her obstetric score would be G3P1A1L2 (Gravida - 3, Para - 1, Abortion - 1, Live birth - 2).

Gravida indicates the number of times a female has been pregnant. It includes present as well as past pregnancy, irrespective of the period of gestation.

Para indicates the number of previous pregnancies that had progressed beyond the period of viability (28 weeks of gestation or more).

Terminologies used in pregnancy:

1. A nullipara is one who has never completed a pregnancy to the stage of viability. She may or may not have aborted previously.
2. A nulligravida is one who is not now and never has been pregnant.
3. A primipara is one who has delivered one viable child. Parity is not increased even if the fetuses are many (twins, triplets).
4. A primigravida is one who is pregnant for the first time.
5. A multigravida is one who has previously been pregnant. She may have aborted or have delivered a viable baby.
6. A multipara is one who has completed two or more pregnancies to the stage of viability or more. A pregnant woman with a previous history of four births or more is called a grand multipara.

It is customary in clinical practice to summarise the past obstetric history by 2 digits

First digit: Number of viable births
Second digit: Number of abortions
Both digits connected with a “+” sign affixing the letter P.
Thus, P1+2 denotes patient had 1 viable birth and 2 abortions.

In this woman, it is denoted as P2+1 as the patient had twin delivery at term and 1 abortion.

In some centres, it is expressed by 4 digits connected by dashes, P(A-B-C-D)
A: Number of term pregnancies (37-42 weeks)
B: Number of preterm pregnancies (28 to less than 37 weeks)
C: Number of miscarriages (less than 28 weeks)
D: Number of children alive at present.

Note: The period of viability is when the fetus is capable of independent existence. The WHO defines it to be 24 weeks while the Indian definition is 28 weeks.

questions.text:
Match the following patients with Uterine prolapse with their best treatment option.

Age/condition
Management

1. Nulliparous women with desire for future pregnancy
2. 45-year-old with no desire for menstruation/pregnancy
3. 30-year-old in puerperial period
4. 38-year-old with family complete but desires for menstruation.

1. Fothergill's operation
2. Cervicopexy
3. Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair
4.  Ring pessary
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1-ii, 2-iii, 3-iv, 4-i

Option C is correct.

Age/condition
Management

1) Nulliparous women with a desire for future pregnancy

ii.  Cervicopexy

2) 45-year-old with no desire for menstruation/pregnancy

iii.  Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair

3) 30-year-old in puerperial period

iv.  Ring pessary

4) 38-year-old with family complete but desires for menstruation.

i.  Fothergill's operation

Sling operations are recommended in cases of nulliparous prolapse for those who wish to retain menstrual and child-bearing function. Mackenrodt’s and uterosacral ligaments of the uterus are strengthened, by using nylon or Dacron tapes as slings. Abdominal sling operations include abdominal wall cervicopexy, Shirodkar’s sling operation, Khanna’s abdominal sling operation, Virkud's sling operation, and Joshi's sling operation.

Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair is the ideal management of genital prolapse in women >40 years of age, those who have completed their families and do not wish to preserve menstrual and child-bearing function.

A ring pessary is used for patients who cannot be surgically managed, such as pregnant patients, patients in puerperium, and very elderly women unfit for surgery. It is used in adjunct with pelvic floor physiotherapy. Pessaries provide mechanical support to the pelvic organs. The first step after fitting the pessary to check if the pessary is adequately retained is to ask the patient to perform Valsalva's manoeuvre or cough and see if the pessary is in place. After being placed, they need to be changed every 3 months.

Fothergill's repair also known as Manchester's operation is suitable for women under 40 years who are desirous of retaining their menstrual and reproductive functions. It involves anterior colporrhaphy with amputation of the cervix. The mackenrodt ligaments are sutured in the front of the cervix and colpoperineorrhaphy is done. It increases the risk of cervical incompetence leading to recurrent abortions and preterm deliveries. Shirodkar's modification of Fothergill's repair avoids cervical amputation, hence subsequent pregnancy complications are avoided.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A pregnant woman at 9 weeks of gestation comes to the clinic. You do a bimanual examination with 2 fingers in the anterior fornix and fingers of other hands behind the uterus. The abdominal and vaginal fingers seem to appose below the body of the uterus. This is called :
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Hegar's sign

The scenario described in the question is the demonstration of Hegar's sign.

Hegar's sign: Bimanual examination with 2 fingers in anterior fornix and fingers of other hands behind the uterus, abdominal and vaginal fingers seem to appose below the body of the uterus which is due to softening of the isthmus.

It is seen during pregnancy at 6-10 wks.

This sign is based on the fact that the upper part of the body of the uterus is enlarged by the growing fetus, the lower part of the body is empty and extremely soft and the cervix is comparatively firm.

Other options :

Option A - Palmer's sign is regular rhythmic uterine contraction during the bimanual examination, which is seen as early as 4-8 weeks.

Option C - Osiander's sign is increased pulsation felt through lateral fornix by 8 weeks.

Option D - Goodell's sign is softening of the cervix by the 6th week.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 35-year-old woman comes with complaints of warty lesions on the vulva. On examination, multiple warty growths on the vulva and around the anal canal are seen. This condition is most likely seen in?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Condyloma accuminata

Multiple warty growths on the vulva and around the anal canal are suggestive of condyloma acuminata (genital warts).

The verrucous growths may appear discrete or coalesce to form large cauliflower-like growths (as shown in the image below). Human papillomaviruses are implicated in causing this condition.

Genital warts:

Genital warts/ venereal warts/ condyloma acuminata are verrucous growths that affect the skin of the labia majora, perineum, perianal region, and vulva. They are most commonly caused by infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) types 6 and 11. The growths may be discrete or coalesce to form cauliflower-like growth. The disease is sexually transmitted. The growth of the warts is favored by vaginal discharge, the use of oral contraceptives, and pregnancy.

HPV causes structural changes in the epithelial cells of the skin. These abnormal epithelial cells are called koilocytes, and their presence is characteristic of HPV infection. The koilocytes have large hyperchromatic nuclei and a perinuclear halo.

Diagnosis is made by colposcopic studies. The lesions on the vulva are stained by toluidine blue. The skin with abnormal nuclei retains the blue dye. These abnormal areas are then biopsied for histopathological examination.

Treatment:

• Local application of podophyllin 25% in alcohol or podophyllin 20% in tincture benzoin or podophyllin cream
• 25% trichloroacetic acid plus 5% fluorouracil
• Diathermy loop, laser ablation, cryotherapy for larger lesions
• Surgical excision
• Interferon ointment or local injection

Option B: Molluscum contagiosum presents as a crop of small domed vesicles with central umbilication. It is caused by the pox virus and it spreads by close sexual or nonsexual contact and by autoinoculation.

Option C: Chancroid appears as small papules that develop into painful ulcerating pustules. They are associated with unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy. It is caused by H. ducreyi.

Option D: Herpes appears as multiple crops of vesicles and ulcers.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 38-year-old woman presents with dysmenorrhoea, menorrhagia, and infertility. After ruling out other possible causes, the gynecologist suspects endometriosis. Which of the following investigations will be most helpful in the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Laparoscopy

In the given clinical scenario, the investigation that will be most helpful in the diagnosis is laparoscopy.

Endometriosis is the presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterus. The patient usually presents with symptoms of abdominal pain, dyspareunia, dysmenorrhea, and infertility. The presence of puckered spots in the posterior fornix is pathognomonic of endometriosis. It is an estrogen-dependent disease of the childbearing age group. The most common site of occurrence is the ovary, followed by the pouch of Douglas.

The gold standard for the diagnosis of endometriosis is visual inspection by laparoscopy, preferably with histological confirmation. Typically, there are small black dots, the so-called powder burns/tattooing seen on the uterosacral ligaments and pouch of Douglas.

Role of laparoscopy in endometriosis:

• To detect and diagnose pelvic endometriosis.
• Locate the site of endometriosis and staging.
• To take biopsy
• To surgically treat endometriosis by ablation, removal.

Other investigations:

• CA-125 levels are raised in endometriosis.
• Monocyte chemotactic protein (MCP-1) levels are raised in the peritoneal fluid of women with endometriosis.
• Transvaginal ultrasound reveals an echo-free cyst, low level echoes or clumps of high-density level echoes representing clots.

The image below shows powder burns/tattooing appearance of endometriosis on diagnostic laparoscopy.

Other options:

Option A: Hysteroscopy and Endometrial Biopsy: These evaluate conditions within the uterine cavity, such as polyps or hyperplasia, but endometriosis involves ectopic endometrial tissue outside the uterus, making this investigation unhelpful for its diagnosis.

Option B: Transvaginal Ultrasound (TVUS): While TVUS can detect ovarian endometriomas, it cannot reliably identify peritoneal or deep infiltrating endometriosis, limiting its utility in providing a comprehensive diagnosis.

Option C: Hysterosalpingography (HSG): This test is primarily used to assess tubal patency and uterine contour in infertility workups but does not provide direct visualization of endometrial implants, making it unsuitable for diagnosing endometriosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of the lab criteria for diagnosis of APLA syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Raised aPTT

Raised aPTT is not a lab criterion for diagnosis of antiphospholipid antibody (APLA) syndrome.

Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome is an autoimmune disorder that is commonly associated with fetal death, preterm delivery, early-onset preeclampsia, and fetal growth restriction due to placental insufficiency and thromboses. Pregnancy loss usually occurs before 10 weeks.

Diagnosis of APLA requires at least 1 clinical criterion and 1 laboratory criterion.

• Obstetric criteria

• One or more unexplained deaths of a morphologically normal fetus at or beyond 10 weeks, or
• Severe preeclampsia or placental insufficiency requiring delivery before 34 weeks, or
• Three or more unexplained consecutive spontaneous abortions before 10 weeks

• Laboratory criteria

• Presence of lupus anticoagulant, or
• Anticardiolipin antibodies, or
• Anti-β2 glycoprotein antibody

Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), also referred to as a recurrent miscarriage or habitual abortion, is historically defined as 3 consecutive pregnancy losses before 20 weeks from the last menstrual period.

Note: The new 2023 ACR/EULAR criteria, is an update from the revised Sapporo criteria with the clinical criteria divided into 6 domains and each metric in the clinical and laboratory value adding a weighted score. This has increased the specificity in diagnosing APS.

questions.text: A 30-year-old G3P2 was admitted to the labor room at 34 weeks of gestation in view of BP - 150/90mmHg and Urine albumin - 2+. Which of the following drugs is not used to control BP in this patient ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Captopril

Captopril is an ACE inhibitor and it is contraindicated in pregnancy.

High BP and proteinuria are diagnostic of pre-eclampsia. Methyl dopa, labetalol, and hydralazine are agents used for the management of pre-eclampsia.

ACE Inhibitor effects on the fetus: These drugs inhibit the conversion of angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin-II. They can cause severe fetal malformations when given in the second and third trimesters.

• Reserpine
• Sodium Nitroprusside (used only as a drug of last resort in refractory severe hypertension)
• Diazoxide

questions.text: What is the average duration of lochial discharge in a puerperal woman?

During early puerperium, sloughing of the decidual tissue causes vaginal discharge which is known as lochia. Most women experience an increase in the amount of bleeding at 7-14 days secondary to the sloughing of the eschar on the placental site. But the average duration of lochial discharge ranges from 24 to 36 days.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The absence of the SRY gene results in which of the following?
options: Development of ovaries and Mullerian system
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Development of ovaries and Mullerian system

The absence of the SRY gene results in the development of the ovaries and the Mullerian system.

In this situation, the gonads will develop into ovaries and the Mullerian duct will differentiate into the uterus, fallopian tubes, and the upper part of the vagina. The master gene responsible for this is the WNT4 gene.

The fate of the Mullerian duct is determined by the presence or absence of the Y chromosome, which has a sex-determining region called the SRY gene.

If the Y chromosome is present, the protein called testis determining factor produced by the SRY gene will lead to the development of testis as the gonads. The Sertoli cells of the testis will then produce Müllerian inhibiting substance (MIS; also known as Anti-Müllerian hormone, AMH) that will cause the Müllerian ducts to regress.

questions.text: Which of the following skin finding in a pregnant woman needs further evaluation?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 2

Image 2 showing acanthosis nigricans is not a normal change seen in pregnancy and hence it needs evaluation if seen in pregnancy. The other images show striae gravidarum, chloasma gravidarum and linea alba which are normal changes seen in pregnancy.

Acanthosis nigricans(AN) is characterized by a symmetrical darkening and thickening of the skin with a velvety texture. More common in the intertriginous areas, mainly the axillae, groins, submammary folds, and neck. Obesity and insulin resistance is the most common association with AN, and it can regress with weight loss. It is more common in patients with darker skin.

Other conditions associated with AN:

• Acromegaly and gigantism
• Diabetes
• HAIR-AN syndrome
• Polycystic ovary syndrome
• Gastric cancer
• Gynaecological cancer

Treatment of the underlying condition is the mainstay. AN associated with obesity responds to dietary restriction and weight loss. The cosmetic appearance of the condition can be treated with topical retinoids or topical keratolytics

Other options:

Option A: Linea nigra is a brownish-black pigmented area that stretches from the xiphisternum to the symphysis pubis in the midline. The pigmentary changes may be due to melanocyte-stimulating hormone from the anterior pituitary. The pigmentation disappears after delivery. Similar changes are observed in women taking oral contraceptives may be due to estrogen and progesterone may be related to it as.

Option C: Striae gravidarum is slightly depressed linear marks with varying length and breadth found in pregnancy. They are predominantly found in the abdominal wall below the umbilicus. They appear pinkish in colour. They can sometimes be found over the thighs and breasts. These stretch marks represent the scar tissues in the deeper layer of the cutis.

Option D: Chloasma gravidarum also called pregnancy mask is an extreme form of pigmentation around the cheek, forehead, and around eyes. It may be patchy or diffuse. It disappears spontaneously after delivery.

Correct answer: D. 300 micrograms

300 microgram is the dose Anti-D which is used for alloimmunization after surgical correction of ectopic pregnancy.

The dose of Anti-D in 1st-trimester abortion and in a surgically treated case of ectopic is 300 micrograms. In 2nd trimester abortion, and in Rh-negative mothers (where it is given within 72 hours of pregnancy termination), the dose is 300 micrograms.

Anti-D is not given when the ectopic is corrected through medical techniques.

Note: 50 micrograms is the minimum dose of Anti-D which can be used for alloimmunization, but 300 micrograms is the recommended dose as per the recent NICE guidelines.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The double decidual sign is seen in:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Intrauterine gestational sac

The double decidual sign is seen in intrauterine pregnancy.

The double decidual sac sign is a useful feature on early pregnancy ultrasound to confirm an early intrauterine pregnancy. It is seen as two concentric rings consisting of outer decidua parietalis and the inner decidua capsularis. The filled head red arrow points to the yolk sac. The presence of the yolk sac confirms the intrauterine location of the pregnancy. It usually appears by the 5th week.

The pseudo gestational sac is a collection of fluid between the endometrial layers, surrounded by a thick decidua. Its presence increases the suspicion of ectopic pregnancy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A lady who is 38 weeks pregnant comes to the OPD for a routine checkup. She has a history of normal twin delivery at term 4 years ago. What is her gravida and para score?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. G2P1

The woman has had two pregnancies in total - the previous twin pregnancy and the current pregnancy, with the first pregnancy resulting in delivery at term. Hence, her obstetric score would be G2P1 (Gravida - 2, Para - 1).

The obstetric score is used to summarise the past obstetric history as follows:

• G - Gravidity, denoting the total number of pregnancies, including the present one
• P - Parity, denoting the total number of pregnancies crossing the period of viability

• This includes both live births and stillbirths
• The current pregnancy is not included

• A - Abortus or the number of pregnancies that were lost for any reason, including induced abortions or miscarriages
• L - Living children.

Multifetal pregnancies count as one for both gravida and para. A pregnant woman who delivers twins for the first time is expressed as primipara.

The GTPAL system includes the following:

• Gravida
• Term (>37 weeks)
• Preterm (20w - 36w 6d)
• Abortions (<20 weeks)
• Number of living children

Note: The period of viability is when the fetus is capable of independent existence. The WHO defines it to be 24 weeks while the Indian definition is 28 weeks.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The most common type of conjoined twins among the given options is _______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Thoracopagus

The most common type of conjoined twins among the given options is thoracophagus.

Based on the parts of the body joined, they are of the following types:

• Ventral

• Rostral

• Omphalopagus (abdomen)
• Thoracopagus (upper chest)
• Cephalopagus (head)

• Caudal

• Ischiopagus (conjoined spines at 180 angles)

• Lateral

• Paraphagus (side-by-side fusion with a shared pelvis)

• Dorsal

• Craniopagus (skull)
• Rachipagus (vertebral arches)
• Pyopagus (pelvis)

Note: The most common type of conjoined twins is parapagus. Since the parapagus is not mentioned in the options, the thoracopagus is the most common among the given options.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is seen in Asherman's syndrome?
options: Low LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol
High LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol
High LH, High FSH, Low estradiol
Normal FSH, Normal LH, Normal estradiol
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Normal FSH, Normal LH, Normal estradiol

Asherman's syndrome has Normal FSH, Normal LH, and Normal estradiol.

Asherman's syndrome is the presence of uterine synechiae, due to the destruction of large areas of the endometrium, most commonly as a result of trauma to the endometrium following pregnancy-related curettages. Oligomenorrhoea, amenorrhoea, dysmenorrhoea, abortion, and infertility are seen with uterine synechiae. The laboratory investigations and hormonal assays are generally normal in isolated cases of uterine synechiae. Diagnosis is generally established using hysteroscopy. Moth-eaten appearance on hysterosalpingography suggests a diagnosis of Asherman syndrome. Treatment is by hysteroscopic adhesiolysis.

Condition
Lab markers

1. Sheehan's syndrome
C. Low LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol

2. Premature Ovarian failure
D. High LH, High FSH, Low estradiol

3. PCOS
B. High LH, Low FSH, Low estradiol

4. Asherman's syndrome
A. Normal FSH, Normal LH, Normal estradiol

Premature Ovarian failure or premature menopause is the development of menopause before the age of 40 years. It is diagnosed when at least 2 serum FSH levels are elevated (>40 mIU/l) when measured at least 1 month apart in a woman <40 years. The other findings consistent with POF include low estradiol and an elevated FSH/LH ratio.

PCOS is a multisystem, metabolic, endocrine dysfunction that commonly occurs among women in the reproductive age group. LH level is raised over 10 IU/mL. FSH level remains normal to low, but FSH/LH ratio falls. Estrone(E1) levels are elevated but estradiol level in PCOS is low in comparison to Estrone (E1).

Sheehan's syndrome/ pituitary apoplexy is hemorrhagic infarction of large pituitary adenomas or pituitary infarction due to traumatic major blood loss. If this blood loss occurs during delivery, it's called Sheehan's syndrome. Affected women may present with panhypopituitarism and may have persistent hypotension, tachycardia, hypoglycemia, and lactation failure. The most prominent symptoms are lactation failure (due to the deficiency of prolactin) and postpartum amenorrhea (due to the deficiency of gonadotropins).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 27-year-old woman presented with itching and malodorous discharge in the vagina which started a week earlier. On examination, the vaginal walls are congested with foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Whiff's test is positive and the gram stain shows the presence of clue cells. This infection is commonly treated with which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Metronidazole

Vaginal itching, foul-smelling frothy vaginal discharge, and a positive Whiff test with clue cells in the gram staining suggest bacterial vaginosis. It is treated with metronidazole.

Bacterial vaginosis:

It is caused due to the alteration in the normal vaginal flora. There is a decrease in the number of lactobacilli. These lactobacilli reduce the pH and release hydrogen peroxide which is antibacterial. Therefore, a decrease in the number of lactobacilli leads to an increase in the number of other organisms like Hemophilus vaginalis, Gardnerella, Mobiluncus, and Mycoplasma hominis.

According to Amsel's criteria, the discharge has the following characteristics.

• White milky non-viscous discharge, adherent to the vaginal wall
• The pH of the discharge is more than 4.5
• Fishy odor when mixed with 10% KOH. This is called the Whiff test.
• Presence of clue cells-the epithelial cells has a fuzzy border due to the adherence of bacteria.
• Decrease in the number of lactobacilli and increase in the number of Gardnerella and other bacteria.

It is treated with 500 mg of metronidazole twice daily for 7 days.

The below image shows the presence of clue cells.

Other options:

Option B: Nystatin pessary is used in the treatment of candidal vaginitis. They present with severe itching, dysuria, and passage of thick curdy discharge. On examination, the vagina is congested and thick curdy discharge can be seen at the vulval mucocutaneous junction and posterior fornix.

Options C and D: Tetracycline and azithromycin are used in the treatment of chlamydial infection. They usually present with vaginal discharge, dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and sometimes cervicitis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
Suitable cases for expectant management in case of placenta previa include:

1. No active vaginal bleeding
2. Duration of pregnancy <37 wk
3. Reactive NST
4. Maternal Hb ≥10 g%
5. Hematocrit value of at least 30%
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are correct

1,2,3,4 and 5 are suitable case for expectant management of placenta previa.

Risk factors for placenta previa

• Multigravida
• Age > 35 years
• Smoking
• Previous cesarean section or myomectomy
• Abnormal placental size and lobes
• Prior curettage

Clinical features of placenta previa:

• Sudden-onset recurrent painless vaginal bleeding: First bleeding usually appears after the end of the second trimester or later and is usually mild and not fatal. This is called ‘Sentinel bleed’.
• The size of the uterus corresponds to gestational age.
• The uterus is relaxed, soft, no tenderness
• Floating head
• Fetal heart sound is present unless there is major separation and the patient is exsanguinated.
• Slowing of fetal heart rate on pressing the head down into the pelvis which recovers promptly as pressure is relieved is suggestive of a low-lying placenta especially of posterior type: Stallworthy sign.

Degree of placenta previa:

There are four types of placenta previa depending upon the degree of extension of the placenta to the lower segment

• Type—I (Low-lying): The major part of the placenta is attached to the upper segment and only the lower margin encroaches onto the lower segment but not up to the internal os.
• Type—II (Marginal): The placenta reaches the margin of the internal os but does not cover it.
• Type—III (Incomplete or partial central): The placenta covers the internal os partially (covers the
internal os when closed but does not entirely do so when fully dilated).
• Type—IV (Central or total): The placenta completely covers the internal os even after it is fully dilated.

Per-Vaginal Examination should not be done in suspected Placenta Previa, whereas it can be only done in the operation theatre with all the arrangements for C-section.

The image below shows the types of placenta previa.

Expectant management for placenta previa was advocated by Macafee and Johnson. The aim is to continue the pregnancy for fetal maturity without compromising maternal health.

Prerequisites

• Availability of blood for transfusion whenever required
• Facilities for cesarean section should be available 24 h.

Suitable cases for expectant management for placenta previa:

• Mother in good health (Hb ≥10 g%; hematocrit ≥30%)
• Duration of pregnancy <37 wk
• No active vaginal bleeding
• Fetal well-being is assured (USG)

Conduct of expectant treatment

• Corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity if <34 wk

• Betamethasone 12mg IM 24 hours apart for 2 doses or
• Dexamethasone 6mg IM 12 hours apart for 4 doses

• Bedrest
• Hb, Blood grouping and urine for protein
• Inspection of vulval pads, fetal surveillance with USG
• Supplementary hematinics
• Rh Immunoglobin should be given to all Rh-negative (unsensitized) women
• Use of tocolytics if there are uterine contractions.

The pregnancy is carried till 37 weeks as part of expectant management. During this time, if there is fetal distress or a bleeding episode, then terminate immediately.

Note - Cervical cerclage is not a part of expectant management

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: After successful delivery of the baby, the obstetrician witnesses that the episiotomy performed has extended backwards beyond the perineal body. Which among the following structures is likely to be injured in this case?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. External anal sphicter

External anal sphincter is the structure injured in an episiotomy extended posteriorly beyond the perineal body.

Perineal tear have been divided into four degrees:

• First degree- laceration is restricted to the skin of the fourchette
• Second degree- muscles of the perineal body are torn through
• Third degree- the tear extends partially backward through the external sphincter of the anus
• Fourth degree- the external anal sphincter is torn and anal mucosa is also involved

A central tear of the perineum is when the head penetrates first through the posterior vaginal wall, then through the perineal body and appears through the skin of the perineum. It usually occurs in patients with a contracted outlet.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 20-year-old nulligravida presented with right flank pain. MRI evaluation revealed a solid, enhancing 5×13×7 cm right ovarian mass. Salpingo-oophorectomy was successfully done and microscopic examination of the tumor cells showed a close resemblance to primordial germ cells. It was also noticed that the tumor appeared histologically identical to a testicular seminoma. Which of the following is not secreted by this tumor?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Sex hormones

An ovarian tumor in a young woman which consists of primordial germ cells and is histologically similar to seminoma suggests a diagnosis of an ovarian dysgerminoma. It does not secrete sex hormones.

Dysgerminoma usually arises in young women or in children, with an average incidence at the age of 20. It is the most common malignant germ cell tumour diagnosed during pregnancy. They are primitive neoplasms that do not have the potential for further differentiation. They are the only germ cell malignancy with a significant rate of bilateral ovarian involvement (15-20%).

The tumor is neutral and does not secrete either male or female sex hormones. It secretes placental alkaline phosphatase (ALP), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and β-hCG. Serum LDH and the isoenzymes LDH-1 and LDH-2 may be used in monitoring individuals or disease recurrence.

Microscopically, there is a monotonous proliferation of large, rounded, polyhedral clear cells that are rich in cytoplasmic glycogen and contain uniform central nuclei with one or a few prominent nucleoli. The tumor cells are histologically identical to the seminoma of the testis. The counterpart of seminoma in females is dysgerminoma.

Treatment involves fertility-sparing surgery with unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. It is highly radiosensitive and has a good prognosis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A lady was discharged after a normal vaginal delivery. On the third day, she presented with seizures, aphasia, and hemiparesis. Which of the following investigations is useful to diagnose this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. MR venography

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of cortical vein thrombosis. This condition can be diagnosed using MR venography.

Cortical vein thrombosis :

Risk factors:

• Pregnancy and puerperium
• Oral contraceptives
• Prothrombotic conditions

Clinical presentation is highly variable. Headache is the most common symptom. Motor or sensory deficits may be seen. Seizures along with focal deficits in the absence of raised intracranial pressure are suggestive of cortical venous thrombosis. Brain MRI with MR venography is a sensitive investigation to diagnose this condition.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A young nulliparous female who desires pregnancy comes to you with complaints of heavy menstrual bleeding. On palpation, an abdominal mass corresponding to 14 weeks of gestation is felt. The mass is found to be a subserosal pedunculated fibroid on imaging. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Myomectomy

The treatment of choice in this nulliparous female with subserosal pedunculated fibroid is myomectomy. Myomectomy is indicated if the uterus size corresponds to more than 12 weeks of gestation and the patient desires pregnancy.

Myomectomy refers to the removal of fibroids and preserving the uterus. It is indicated in fibroids which present with the following

• Persistent uterine bleeding despite medical therapy
• Excessive pain or pressure symptoms
• Size > 12 weeks, patient desirous to have a baby
• Unexplained infertility with distortion of the uterine cavity due to fibroid
• Recurrent pregnancy wastage due to fibroid
• Rapid growth during follow up
• Subserous pedunculated fibroid

Myomectomy can be performed by laparoscopy, hysteroscopy, or laparotomy. It is contraindicated in patients with an infected fibroid, pelvic or endometrial tuberculosis, suspected malignancy, and growth in post-menopausal and multiparous women where hysterectomy can be the safe definitive management.

Fibroids are benign estrogen dependant tumors of the uterine smooth muscles and connective tissue.

Management of uterine fibroids in asymptomatic patients includes observation with regular follow-up regardless of the size of the fibroid. Surgery is indicated in cornual fibroids if it causes infertility or pedunculated fibroids (due to the risk of torsion).

In symptomatic patients, medical therapy is done to shrink the fibroid. It acts as a preoperative adjunct. Surgical methods such as myomectomy, laparoscopic myolysis, hysterectomy, and endometrial ablation are tried for patients with persistent symptoms despite conservative management. Hysterectomy is done in postmenopausal women and in multiparous women who have completed their families or are not desirous of childbirth.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A P5 female bleeds profusely after delivery of the placenta. You initiate IV fluids with oxytocin. However, the patient continues to bleed over the next 10 min even after adequate uterine massage. On examination, she is tachycardic, hypotensive and the uterus is soft and boggy. What is the next step of management?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Carry out balloon tamponade

The next step of management is to carry out balloon tamponade.

• When the uterine bleeding is unresponsive to uterotonic agents, bimanual uterine compression can be performed, IV lines must be placed and volume resuscitation started.
• A Bakri postpartum balloon may be inserted and inflated to tamponade the endometrial cavity.

Other options mentioned are surgical methods of management. These are tried after all forms of medical management have failed.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 32-year-old primigravida with twin gestation presents to the clinic in active labor. The first baby is in breech presentation and the second baby is in cephalic presentation. What is the best step of management in this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Cesarean section

In this scenario, since the first twin is in breech (non-cephalic presentation), the best step of management is to deliver through cesarean section.

Scheme of management of twins in labor:

1. If the first twin/ both twins are in the non-cephalic presentation: deliver through cesarean section.

2. If the first twin is in vertex presentation: Deliver the first twin through vaginal delivery and do not give methergine post-delivery of the first baby. Delivering the second twin, If it is in,

• Breech: Deliver through breech extraction
• Transverse lie

• If the obstetrician is skilled in podalic version: Internal podalic version and breech extraction under GA.
• If the obstetrician is unskilled: External version into a longitudinal lie preferably cephalic or if that fails podalic.

• Vertex: Vaginal delivery, assisted forceps/ventouse.

Cesarean delivery of the breech fetus is indicated in the following:

• Twins, with the first baby in the breech
• Large fetus: >3800 to 4000 g
• Apparently healthy and viable preterm fetus either with active labor or with indicated delivery
• Severe IUGR
• Footling presentation (due to risk of cord prolapse)
• Hyperextended head
• Contracted pelvis
• Prior cesarean delivery
• Preterm breech

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A middle-aged woman complains of urine dribbling from the vagina. On further examination and investigation, she is diagnosed with a vesicovaginal fistula. Which of the following is false about the management of her condition?
options: Latzko procedure is suited for post-hysterectomy fistula, caused by cancer cervix
Following a failed attempt, a second attempt can be made after 4 weeks
Continous bladder drainage required for 14 days postoperatively
Sexual abstinence for 3 months is advised after the surgery
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Following a failed attempt, a second attempt can be made after 4 weeks

In case the fistula repair fails, a second attempt is made only after 3 months.

Vesicovaginal fistula(VVF) is a type of genital fistula, which is an abnormal communication between the genital tract and the urinary tract. It occurs mostly due to obstetric injuries such as prolonged labor, and instrumental or manipulative deliveries. Patients present with true incontinence characterized by constant dribbling of urine.

Small fistulas due to difficult childbirth can heal spontaneously. In the case of an established fistula, it is better to wait for about 3 months for all tissue inflammation to subside, before surgery is undertaken. Most vesicovaginal fistulas are repaired per vaginally. The various surgeries done for the repair of VVF are as follows:

• Latzko procedure: It is done by denudation of vaginal epithelium around fistulous edges and approximation of raw surface with absorbable sutures. This technique is suited for post-hysterectomy fistula that is caused by cancer cervix (Option A). It can lead to narrowing of the vagina or vaginal atresia. Fistula located at the vaginal vault, post hysterectomy is the most difficult to treat, this technique is suited for such cases.
• Chassar-Moir technique: Here, the vagina and bladder are separated and sutured into two layers taking care to avoid tension and overlapping suture lines.
• Ureteric implantation into the sigmoid colon in case previous surgeries fail.

Post-operatively, continuous bladder drainage for 14 days (Option C) along with antibiotics is recommended. Vaginal or speculum examination and intercourse are not advised for 3 months after surgery (Option D). Avoiding pregnancy for a year is also recommended. A cesarean section is usually done for future pregnancies.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The following instrument is used to augment labour in a 28-year-old primigravida via low rupture of membranes. Identify this instrument.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Kocher's artery forceps

The given instrument is Kocher's artery forceps and is identified by the presence of a single tooth at the tip.

Kocher's artery forceps are used to achieve hemostasis by holding bleeding vessels. They are also used in low rupture of membranes to augment labour or for the surgical induction of labour.

The difference between artery forceps and needle holders is in the edge and smoothness of corrugations. Artery forceps have smooth edges and single lined corrugations whereas, needle holders have rough edges and crossed lines forming square to diamond shaped corrugations.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Identify the given image based on the Doppler findings.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Reversed end-diastolic flow

The umbilical artery Doppler depicts the reversal of end-diastolic flow (waves appearing below the baseline) which is seen in intrauterine growth restriction.

Abnormal flow patterns in the umbilical artery:

Reduced End diastolic flow: Uteroplacental insufficiency (S/D ratio increases)

Absent End diastolic flow: Fetal compromise - terminate the pregnancy by cesarean section if >34 weeks.

Reverse end diastolic flow: Impending doom of death - terminate pregnancy irrespective of gestational age.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 33-week pregnant woman with pre-eclampsia presents with clinical features suggestive of HELLP syndrome. What is the best management approach?
options: Give steroids and wait till 37 weeks
Give MgSo4 and deliver at 36 weeks
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Termination of pregnancy

The definitive management of PIH/eclampsia is termination of pregnancy only.

Indications for termination of pregnancy, irrespective of gestational age, in cases of pre-eclampsia are as follows:

• Severe pre-eclampsia
• Eclampsia (give MgSO4 followed by induction of labor)
• HELLP syndrome
• Pulmonary edema
• Significant renal dysfunction, coagulopathy
• Fetal compromise

Other options:

Option B: Give steroids and wait till 37 weeks: This would be the answer if it were mild pre-eclampsia. Here, it is a case of severe pre-eclampsia with HELLP syndrome.

Option C: Give MgSo4 and deliver at 36 weeks: MgSO4 is given for prophylaxis of eclampsia in patients with severe pre-eclampsia and pregnancy is terminated at >34 weeks. If 27-34 weeks, give corticosteroids and deliver after 24 hours of the last dose of steroid.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 56-year-old multiparous woman presented with grade II/III uterine prolapse with cystocele. She complains of passing urine on coughing and sneezing. What is the type of urinary incontinence seen in this patient?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Stress incontinence

The type of urinary incontinence present in a patient with prolapse and cystocele experiencing urination on coughing and sneezing is stress incontinence.

Stress incontinence refers to the involuntary leakage of urine when there is increased intraabdominal pressure (eg, coughing, sneezing, laughing, Valsalva maneuver). There is an absence of detrusor muscle contraction, seen in urodynamic studies.

Causes:

• Age and menopause - due to estrogen deficiency
• Multiparity - due to loss of pelvic muscle tone
• Obesity
• Smoking
• Constipation, chronic cough
• Pelvic organ prolapse
• Pregnancy - due to the effect of progesterone and pressure of the gravid uterus on the bladder neck.
• Puerperium - due to descent of the bladder neck, loss of urethro-vesical angle, and reduced pelvic muscle tone
• Surgical repair of vesicovaginal fistula

Grading of genuine stress incontinence (GSI) :

• Grade I: Incontinence with only severe stress, such as coughing, sneezing, and jogging.
• Grade II: Incontinence with moderate stress, such as fast walking, and going up and down the stairs.
• Grade III: Incontinence with mild stress such as standing.

Investigations are only done prior to surgery to confirm the diagnosis. They include the stress test, cotton swab or Q tip test, Marshall and Bonney’s test, urethroscopy, and urodynamic studies. These are not required prior to conservative management.

Conservative management includes Kegel's pelvic exercises, electric nerve stimulation, devices like pessaries, vaginal cones, and artificial sphincters. Medical treatment with estrogen creams, anti-adrenergic, venlafaxine, and imipramine may be useful.

Other options:

Option A: Overflow incontinence is an old term that refers to the inability to empty the bladder, with involuntary, continuous urinary dribbling. Currently, it refers to another presentation of urge incontinence.

Option B: Urge incontinence is the involuntary escape of urine when there is an imminent need to urinate. It occurs due to detrusor muscle overactivity or detrusor instability. It is seen more commonly in old women with decreased bladder capacity, decreased sensation, and central nervous system (CNS) inhibition.

Option D: Neurogenic bladder occurs in patients with neurogenic dysfunction leading to detrusor hyperreflexia. Conditions such as multiple sclerosis, stroke, Parkinson's disease, and spinal injury give rise to this. They present with urgency or urge incontinence.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following types of morbidly adherent placenta is shown in the given image?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Placenta increta

The given image shows placental tissue invading the myometrium of the uterus suggestive of placenta increta.

Morbidly adherent placenta occurs due to the partial or total absence of the decidua basalis and imperfect development of the fibrinoid or Nitabuch layer. It is of three types:

• Placenta accreta - villi are attached to the myometrium.
• Placenta increta - villi invade deep into the myometrium.
• Placenta percreta - villi penetrate through the entire myometrium and to or through the serosa.

Based on the adherence of placental lobules, all three types of morbidly adherent placenta can be:

• Total - involving all lobules of the placenta
• Focal - involving a single lobule or part of a lobule of the placenta

Morbidly adherent placenta can lead to torrential post-partum hemorrhage. It is managed via C-section and peripartum hysterectomy.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A teenager presented with complaints of excessive growth of coarse hair on her jawline and upper lip. Which of the following is the most common cause for this condition?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS)

The given clinical history of excessive growth of coarse hair is suggestive of hirsutism. The most common cause for hirsutism in female patients is polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS).

Hirsutism is defined as excessive growth of androgen-dependent sexual hair or male distribution of hair in female patients. PCOS accounts for 70-80% of the cases of hirsutism, which typically begins in late adolescence or the early 20s.

Idiopathic hirsutism is the second most frequent cause. The most common rapid onset of hirsutism in young females is a testosterone-producing tumour like granulosa cell or Sertoli-Leydig cell tumours.

Other less common causes of hirsutism include:

• Late-onset congenital adrenal hyperplasia
• Tumours of the ovary and adrenal gland
• Cushing’s syndrome
• Drug-induced

Virilisation: Characterized by more extensive androgen-induced changes than hirsutism alone. It has the following features:

• Acne
• Increased oily skin
• Temporal balding
• Clitoromegaly
• Deepening of the voice
• Development of male muscular pattern and body habitus
• Atrophy of breasts

Hypertrichosis: Excessive growth of non-sexual hair.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A primigravida was admitted in labor at 38 weeks of gestation. In view of the prolonged second stage of labor, a mediolateral episiotomy was given to aid instrumental delivery. It is usually angled at ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 60 degrees

The mediolateral episiotomy is angled at 60°.

Episiotomy is a surgically planned incision on the perineum and the posterior vaginal wall during the second stage of labour. It is done to

• To enlarge the vaginal introitus so as to facilitate easy and safe delivery of the fetus.
• To minimize overstretching and rupture of the perineal muscles and fascia
• To reduce the stress and strain on the fetal head.

It is given during crowning when the head is visible. There are many types like median, mediolateral, lateral and j shaped. Among these, mediolateral episiotomy is preferred.

The mediolateral episiotomy begins at the midline of the fourchette and is directed to the right or left at an angle 60 degrees off the midline. This angle accounts for stretch distortion of perineal anatomy during crowning. After delivery and distortion resolution, it ultimately yields an incision 45-degrees from the midline.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 24-year-old Rh-negative G2P1 mother was delivered by cesarean section at 37 weeks gestation. The baby is found to be Rh-positive. To access fetomaternal transfusion a Kleihaeur Betke test was done which detected 20 ml of fetal RBCs. What is the dose of anti-D that should be administered to the mother? (Assume fetal hematocrit to be 50 percent)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 400 µg

10 µg of anti-D is required for every 1 mL of fetal whole blood or 0.5 mL of fetal RBCs.Hence for 20 mL of fetal RBCs, 400 µg of anti-D should be administered.

Kleihauer–Betke test is the most commonly used quantitative test for measuring the fetal red cells in the maternal circulation. The reagent used for the Kleihauer–Betke test is citric acid. It is also known as the acid elution test.

Principle: Fetal erythrocytes contain hemoglobin F, which is more resistant to acid elution than hemoglobin A in the maternal erythrocytes.

After exposure to acid, only fetal hemoglobin remains, such that after staining, the fetal erythrocytes appear red and adult cells appear as ghosts. These fetal cells are counted per 50 low-power fields. If there are 80 fetal erythrocytes in 50 low-power fields in maternal peripheral blood films, it represents a transplacental hemorrhage to the extent of 4 mL of fetal blood. 10 µg of anti-D is required for every 1 mL of fetal whole blood or 0.5 mL of fetal RBCs.

Fetomaternal hemorrhage can also be quantified using flow cytometry to measure red cell size. It is unaffected by maternal levels of fetal hemoglobin F or by fetal levels of hemoglobin A. Flow cytometry has been reported to be more sensitive and accurate than the Kleihaeur Betke test.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A young woman, who was diagnosed with threatened abortion was referred to you from the peripheral hospital for an USG (Ultrasonography). Examination of this patient would reveal:
options: Closed cervical os with absent fetal cardiac activity on USG
Closed cervical os with fetal cardiac activity on USG
Dilated cervical os with absent fetal cardiac activity on USG
Dilated cervical os with fetal cardiac activity on USG
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Closed cervical os with fetal cardiac activity on USG

Examination of a patient diagnosed with threatened abortion would reveal closed cervical os with fetal cardiac activity on USG.

In threatened miscarriage, the process of miscarriage has started but has not progressed to a state from which recovery is impossible.

Features:

• Bleeding which is usually slight and may be brownish or bright red in color
• Usually painless but pain appears following hemorrhage
• Closed external os
• Uterine size corresponds to the period of amenorrhea
• Uterus and cervix feel soft
• Transvaginal Ultrasonography shows well-formed gestation ring indicating healthy fetus with fetal cardiac activity.

Abortion is the expulsion or extraction from the mother of an embryo or fetus weighing 500 g or less when it is not capable of independent survival.

Classification of abortion:

Other options:

Option A: In missed abortion, the fetus is dead and is retained inside the uterus for a variable period. Here closed cervical os with absent fetal cardiac activity on USG can be seen.

Option C: In incomplete abortion, entire products of conception are not expelled, instead, a part of it is left inside the uterine cavity. Here dilated cervical os with absent fetal cardiac activity on USG can be seen.

Option D: In inevitable abortion, the changes have progressed to a state from where continuation of pregnancy is impossible. Here dilated cervical os with fetal cardiac activity on USG can be seen.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 30-year-old woman presents with severe dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia and infertility. A diagnosis of endometriosis was made and she was posted for laparoscopy surgery. During the procedure, dense pelvic adhesions were seen with the bowel stuck to the fundus and cystic ovaries stuck to each other. What is the next step in managing this patient?
options: Gestrinone to decrease the LH surge
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Cystectomy and adhesiolysis

The clinical scenario is suggestive of endometriosis and the next step in the management of this patient is cystectomy and adhesiolysis.

After the surgery the patient is advised to start infertility treatment too.

Medical management of endometriosis:

• Gestrinone is an anti-estrogenic, anti-progestational, and mildly anabolic drug that reduces sex-hormone-binding globulin to release free testosterone. It also decreases the LH surge. It causes regression of lesions and amenorrhea. It is a 19-nortestosterone derivative similar to danazol, but with fewer side effects.
• Combined oral contraceptives are used for symptom control and alleviate disease. These also cause menstrual cycle regulation and delay pregnancy.
• Oral progestogens exert an anti-estrogenic effect and cause decidualization and endometrial atrophy. This causes disease regression. It doesn't prevent ovulation, thus is suitable for women who are trying to conceive.
• Mirena IUCDs reduce dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia. It is a single-sitting treatment with minimal side effects.
• Aromatase inhibitors like letrozole are anti-estrogens given for disease regression.
• Anti-inflammatory drugs like mefenamic acid and naproxen relieve dysmenorrhea.

Therapeutic procedures:

• Aspiration of Peritoneal fluid from the cul-de-sac removes PGE2, relieves dysmenorrhea, pelvic pain, and improves fertility
• Destruction of endometriotic lesions <3cm with diathermy, Nd-YAG laser or CO2 vaporization can be attempted.
• Larger lesions and chocolate cysts can be excised.
• Cystectomy can be done for pelvic pain but can reduce fertility potential.
• Laparoscopic breaking of adhesions relieves dysmenorrhea and chronic pelvic pain. It also restores tubal patency and improves ovulation. Pre-sacral neurectomy can be done simultaneously..
• Laser uterosacral nerve ablation (LUNA) is done for pelvic pain.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: What is the cause of lactational amenorrhea?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Increased prolactin secretion

The cause of lactational amenorrhea is increased prolactin secretion as a result of the baby sucking at the mother's breast.

Lactational amenorrhea:

• Type of secondary amenorrhea due to the effect of prolactin secretion.
• During lactation, there are pulsatile bursts of prolactin secretion in response to suckling.
• Prolactin suppresses GnRH, LH, and FSH causing lactational amenorrhea.
• Regular lactation with one feed at night delays ovulation and pregnancy for up to 6 months, provided she remains amenorrhoeic.
• After 6 months, lactation has no bearing on ovulation and pregnancy can occur, despite amenorrhoea and might need other forms of contraception.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: The image given below depicts which abnormality of the placenta?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Placenta succenturiata

The given image depicts placenta succenturiata in which one or more small lobes of placenta may be placed at a distance from main placental margin.

Its complications are

• Postpartum hemorrhage
• Subinvolution
• Uterine sepsis
• Polyp formation

Other options:

• Battledore placenta – The cord is attached to the margin of the placenta.

• Circumvallate placenta - The fetal surface of placenta is covered by a white ring at the periphery made up of a double fold of amnion and chorion.

• Velamentous cord insertion - The umbilical cord is attached to the fetal membranes. The cord vessels traverse between the membranes for some distance before reaching the placenta.

questions.text: A 22-year-old infertile male underwent semen analysis. Results show: sperm concentration: 10 million/ml; pH: 7.5; volume: 2 mL. The most likely diagnosis is ______
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Oligospermia

This male, with a sperm concentration of 10 million/mL, has findings suggestive of oligospermia.

According to the WHO 2010 criteria for semen analysis, the lower reference limit for normal sperm concentration is 15 million/mL. Concentrations of 16 million/mL is Normospermia (Option A)

Oligospermia is defined as a sperm concentration <15 million/mL, and counts <5 million/mL are considered severe.

Morphology is the most important factor/marker of sperm analysis.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 26 year old woman, G2P1, is informed after her first trimester scan , that the fetus has open spina bifida. At 30 weeks of gestation, her USG scan would most likely report:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Single deepest vertical pocket = 9 cm

According to the given clinical vignette, at 30 weeks of gestation, her USG scan would most likely report a single deepest vertical pocket of 9 cm in a fetus with open spina bifida.

Spina bifida is one of the causes of polyhydramnios which is diagnosed when the single deepest vertical pocket (DVP) is greater than 8 cm.

Open spina bifida causes increased transudation from the meninges , leading to increasing amounts of liquor amnii production i.e. polyhydramnios.

Polyhydramnios is diagnosed when :

• Amniotic fluid index (AFI) is greater than 24cm
• Single deepest vertical pocket  (DVP) is greater than 8 cm
• Amniotic fluid volume is greater than 2L

Other options :

Option A : AFI=4 cm implies oligohydramnios (AFI< 5 cm or DVP< 2cm).

Option B: DVP=2 cm implies oligohydramnios.

Option C : AFI = 10 cm implies normal AFI (5-25 cm).

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following features can be seen in a patient with cervical incompetence?
options: Repeated third trimester painless cervical dilatation
Bleeding per vaginum in the first trimester
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Repeated mid-trimester painless cervical dilatation

Cervical incompetence or insufficiency is characterized by repeated mid-trimester painless cervical dilatation. Escape of amniotic fluid followed by painless expulsion of products of conception can also be seen.

Risk factors for cervical incompetence:

• Congenital uterine anomalies
• Acquired -

• Dilatation and currettage
• Dilatation and evacuation
• Vaginal operative delivery through an undilated cervix
• Amputation of cervix

• Multiple gestations
• Prior preterm birth

Cervical incompetence or insufficiency is a functional or anatomical impairment in the retentive power of the cervix (or internal os). It is characterized by repeated, mid-trimester painless cervical dilatation. It leads to the escape of amniotic fluid followed by painless expulsion of the products of conception.

Cerclage is the procedure done to strengthen the cervix in patients with cervical incompetence. Contraindications of cervical cerclage include:

• Ruptured membranes
• Intrauterine infection
• Uterine contractions
• Vaginal bleeding
• Cervical dilatation >4 cm
• Fetal death or defect

Cervical incompetence is associated with various risk factors such as prior preterm birth, congenital uterine anomalies, iatrogenic (dilatation and curettage, induced abortion by dilatation and evacuation, vaginal operative delivery through an undilated cervix, amputation of the cervix, etc), and multiple gestations.

In the interconceptional period, diagnosis is made with the passage of number 6-8 Hegar's dilator beyond the internal os without resistance or pain. Investigations for cervical incompetence during pregnancy include:

• Per speculum examination - shows cervical dilatation with herniation of membranes
• Transvaginal ultrasound - funneling of internal os >1 cm and cervical length <25 mm

Prophylactic cervical cerclage is done between 12-14 weeks of gestation. Rescue or emergency cerclage is done when there is bulging or prolapse of membranes through a dilated cervix.

Shirodkar and McDonald's methods of cervical cerclage are the commonly performed cerclage procedures during pregnancy. In McDonald's method, a non-absorbable (mersilene) suture material is placed as a purse-string suture at the level of the internal os, whereas in the Shirodkar method, non-absorbable (mersilene) tape is used. Removal of stitch should be done at the 37th week of gestation. It can be removed earlier in case of preterm labor or if signs of abortion are seen. Laparoscopic abdominal cerclage is used for non-pregnant patients.
